NASHR:v2p133/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p133/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p133/r4.claim: Some Iraqi transmitters wrongly report that al-Kisāʾī alone pauses on مناة with hāʾ and the others with tāʾ; they mistook Nusayr's report of spelling for a reading.
NASHR:v2p133/r4.anchor: وشذ جماعة من العراقيين فرووا عن الكسائي وحده الوقف على مناة بالهاء

NASHR:v2p133/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p133/r5.speaker: الأهوازي
NASHR:v2p133/r5.claim: Al-Ahwāzī says the codices write منوة with wāw and all readers pause with tāʾ; the author says every reader pauses with hāʾ according to the written form.
NASHR:v2p133/r5.anchor: والعجب من قول الأهوازي: وأجمعت المصاحف

ELMALILI:53:23-25/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r1.claim: Garânīq is gurnûk or gurneyk, a long-necked white water bird larger than a goose; the word also describes a beautiful young woman and soft wind-moved hair.
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r1.anchor: Garânîk”, müfredi “gurnûk”, “gurneyk” kuğu kuşu denilen beyaz bir su kuşudur ki kazdan büyük uzun boyunlu güzel endamlı bir kuştur.

ELMALILI:53:23-25/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r2.claim: The word can also mean a fair, beautiful, full-bodied young woman, or soft hair stirred by a pleasant breeze.
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r2.anchor: Nesîm-i dilküşâ estikçe deprenip oynayan yumuşak saçlara da “garânika” ve “garânikiyye” denilir.

ELMALILI:53:23-25/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r3.claim: Polytheists poetically likened their white stone idols to high-flying gharaniq, called them God's daughters, and hoped for their intercession.
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r3.anchor: İşte müşrikler beyaz taşlardan yapılan putlarını böyle şâirâne bir teşbih ile yüksekte uçan garânîka benzeterek Allah’ın kızları diye şefaatlerini umduklarından

ELMALILI:53:23-25/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r11.claim: The idols named with these feminine titles possess none of the reality or qualities implied by divinity, honor, relation to God, or intercession; they are empty names.
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r11.anchor: ulûhiyet, izzet, Allah’a nisbet, şefaat gibi mefhumları tahakkuk ettirecek hiçbir haysiyeti hâiz değil {إِلَّآ أَسْمَآءٌۭ} sâde kuru isimlerden ibarettirler.

ELMALILI:53:23-25/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r12.claim: The feminine pronoun first evokes the idols with their asserted traits, then strips those traits away and underscores that nothing remains but names, refuting the gharaniq claim too.
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r12.anchor: Bu sebeple burada bu müennes هِىَ zamiri merci‘i itibariyle bize bir nükte ifade etmektedir.

ELMALILI:53:23-25/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r13.speaker: Taberî ve Zemahşerî gibi bazı müfessirler
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r13.claim: Some exegetes report that Satan inserted a line praising the gharaniq during the Prophet's recitation of al-Najm, after which God abrogated it and confirmed the revelation.
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r13.anchor: Taberî ve Zemahşerî gibi bazı müfessirler kendilerine yakışmayan bir قِيل söylemişler; güya Ve’n-Necmi Sûresi nâzil olup da

ELMALILI:53:23-25/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r14.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r14.claim: Abu Hayyan says Ibn Ishaq regarded the story as a fabrication of heretics and wrote a book about it.
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r14.anchor: Ebû Hayyân rahmetullahi aleyh der ki: “Bu kıssa, sîret-i nebeviye câmi‘i İmam Muhammed b. İshak’tan sual edildiğinde zenâdıkanın vaz‘ından olduğunu söylemiş

ELMALILI:53:23-25/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r15.speaker: Beyhâkī
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r15.claim: Bayhaqi says the report is not established, its transmitters are criticized, it is absent from sound collections, and it must be rejected.
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r15.anchor: İmam Hâfız Ebû Bekir Ahmed b. Hüseyn-i Beyhâkī dahi demiştir ki: ‘Bu kıssa nakil cihetinden sâbit değildir. Râvîleri mat‘ûndur.

ELMALILI:53:23-25/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r16.claim: Yaqut reports that polytheists used the gharaniq formula while circumambulating the Kaaba, so the simile predates Muhammad and was originally their satanic suggestion.
ELMALILI:53:23-25/r16.anchor: Demek ki garânîk teşbîhi Peygamber’den evvel söylenegelmiş bir sözdür.

ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r2.claim: If the disputed words were uttered, they could only be a narration of pagan speech: after the rebuke they would form a coherent quotation immediately debunked as empty names, whereas inserting them after Manat would disrupt the cadence.
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r2.anchor: eğer söylenmiş olsa idi yakışan tam burada yani تِلْكَ إِذًۭا قِسْمَةٌۭ ضِيزَىٰٓ’den sonra إِنْ هِىَ’den evvel söylenmek lâzım gelirdi.

ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r3.claim: The passage already rejects hoped-for intercession: the later statement that angels in heaven cannot avail by their intercession makes this intended meaning clear even without an explicit quotation.
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r3.anchor: aşağıda وَكَم مِّن مَّلَكٍۢ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ لَا تُغْنِى شَفَٰعَتُهُمْ âyetinde bilhassa bu şefaat mazmûnuna ilişileceği cihetle

ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r4.claim: The words “you and your fathers named them” mean they falsely gave idols names without the realities those names claim to express.
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r4.anchor: Onlara o isimleri siz ve babalarınız taktınız ifade ettikleri mefhumlardan hiçbiri bulunmaksızın o putlara o isimleri siz ve babalarınız yalan olarak verdiniz.

ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r5.claim: God sent no authority, proof, or effective meaning that could justify those names, so they have no true referents.
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r5.anchor: Allah onlara öyle bir saltanat indirmedi öyle bir tesmiyeye hak verdirecek hiçbir burhan,

ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r6.claim: The shift from direct address to third person signals that the idolaters are not fit recipients of direct address as their conduct is explained.
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r6.anchor: bunu beyan sırasında onların hitâba kābil olmadıklarına tenbih için hitabdan gıyâba geçilerek buyuruluyor ki

ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r7.claim: They follow conjecture and their lower selves' desires, pursuing empty fantasies and wishes instead of seeking truth and good in belief and practice.
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r7.anchor: İtikad ve amellerinde hak ve hayrı aramıyorlar. Dini mücerred nefsin hevâ ve hevesiyle hissiyâtından ibaret imiş gibi farzederek nefs-i emmârelerinin meylettiği boş, mânasız, hayâlât ile kuru temenniyât peşinde gidiyorlar.

ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r8.claim: God sent the Prophet and Qur'an as guidance to the path of truth and certainty, yet they still follow conjecture and hope for idols' intercession.
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r8.anchor: yani zann u hevâ ile murâda erilemeyeceğini anlatan ve murâda doğru ermek için tâkip edilmesi lâzım gelen hak ve yakīn yolunu gösteren Peygamber ve Kur’an Allah tarafından gelmiş iken

ASAD-NOTES:53:21#n15/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:21#n15/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:21#n15/r1.claim: Asad points readers to 12:40 as a parallel on the invented divine names and lack of warrant.

ASAD-NOTES:53:21#n16/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:21#n16/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:21#n16/r1.claim: The alleged mediation of goddesses and angels is wishful thinking; Asad says the same idea persists in saint veneration and the deification of people in higher religions.
ASAD-NOTES:53:21#n16/r1.anchor: those goddesses, as well as the angels, would act as "mediators" between their worshippers and God: a wishful idea which lingers on even among adherents of higher religions

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r2.claim: Although the named idols foreground Quraysh, the argument condemns deviations throughout history that damage monotheism and enslave people to created, ordinary things; shirk beliefs and conduct lack a sound knowledge source.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r2.anchor: insanlık tarihi boyunca görülegelen, biçimleri farklı olsa da, tevhid inancını zedelemesi ve insanı yaratılmışlara, alelâde varlıklara kul etmesi açısından özde bu tip davranış biçimiyle örtüşen bütün itikadî sapkınlıkların mahkûm edilmesinin hedeflendiği anlaşılmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r3.claim: Claims about God’s attributes and how His lordship is expressed require direct contact with God or knowledge from a messenger authorized by Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r3.anchor: Allah’ın sıfatları ve rubûbiyyetini nasıl ortaya koyduğu hususunda bir iddiada bulunabilmesi ancak O’nunla doğrudan temas kurabilmesine veya O’nun tarafından yetkilendirilmiş bir elçiden bilgi almasına bağlıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r4.claim: Polytheists say idols bring them nearer to God, admitting no direct contact, yet do not claim revelation as the source of their beliefs; they had even wished for a prophet and divine book.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r4.anchor: Müşrikler ise putların kendilerini Allah’a yaklaştıracağını umduklarını söylüyor, böylece Allah ile doğrudan temas kuramadıklarını itiraf etmiş oluyorlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r5.claim: With no revealed source claimed, rational scrutiny is all that remains, and the verses expose their failure through a simple line of reasoning.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r5.anchor: Böyle bir durumda geriye sadece söylenenlerin ve yapılanların aklî muhâkemeye vurulması kalmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r6.claim: They have no reliable source for saying angels are God’s daughters or assigning names to their fabricated gods, and instead follow personal desires and the ease of blind imitation rather than using reason.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r6.anchor: Onlar melekleri Allah’ın çocukları sayarken, üstelik O’na ortak koştukları düzmece tanrılara isim koyarken bilgi kaynakları nedir?

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r7.claim: They fail to see the absurd contradiction of claiming male children for themselves while assigning to God the female sex they belittle.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r7.anchor: erkek çocukları kendilerine, akıllarınca küçümseyip horladıkları kadın cinsini ise Allah’a ayırmanın ne kadar saçma ve çelişkili olduğunu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r19.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r19.claim: Verses 23 and 28 say that those who associate partners with God rely on conjecture rather than sound knowledge.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r19.anchor: Allah’a ortak koşanların sağlam bir bilgiye değil zanna dayandıkları belirtilmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r20.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r20.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r20.claim: Verse 23 adds that they follow personal desires even in religious matters, acting from subjective motives; here conjecture means acting on guesses and fantasies without sound methods of knowledge, especially about faith.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r20.anchor: dinî meselelerde bile kişisel arzularına uyduklarına, dolayısıyla sübjektif âmillerle hareket ettiklerine değinilmekte ve bu tutumları eleştirilmektedir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r1.claim: The Makkan idols are inventions of fancy without reality or divine sanction; reason, instinct, and intellect cannot affirm them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r1.anchor: their false idols, on the basis of which they are denying the warnings

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r2.claim: Idolaters follow conjecture and baseless wishes despite manifest guidance; desire cannot replace truth, and they will face the warned facts rather than what they wish for.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r2.anchor: conjectures and suppositions cannot take the place of truth, and false wishes and desires have no basis

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r3.claim: The Makkan adversaries cannot rely on self-claimed deities to escape fear of Judgment: Lāt, Manāt, and ʿUzzā are merely hypothetical names without real-world referents.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r3.anchor: they are merely hypothetical names which qualify no one in the real world

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r4.claim: Reward and punishment are realities, and conjecture or wishes cannot overcome them; all affairs of heaven and earth remain in God's hands.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r4.anchor: Reward and punishment is a reality. They cannot combat reality with conjecture

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p53/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p53/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p53/r6.claim: The deities are invented names given by the people and their forefathers, with no real beings corresponding to them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p53/r6.anchor: they are merely names which they and their forefathers have given them and they do not represent any one in the real world.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p53/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p53/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p53/r7.claim: The deities have no divine sanction; ancestral practice proves nothing because those ancestors also worshipped by blindly following their forebears.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p53/r7.anchor: If they have found their forefathers worshipping them, then this is not reason enough.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p53/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p53/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p53/r8.claim: A valid sanction could come from human nature and intellect, God's signs in the outer and inner worlds, or direct communication through prophets and messengers; no such sanction exists here.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p53/r8.anchor: God’s sanction in this regard could have been found in human nature and intellect or could have been found in God’s signs

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p53/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p53/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p53/r9.claim: Had God endorsed these deities, He could have named them beloved daughters whose intercession He always accepts and whose worshippers He forgives, but He did not.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p53/r9.anchor: He could have said that such and such are his favourite daughters whose recommendation He always accepts

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r1.claim: The shift from direct to indirect address rebukes the people's deprivation and intellectual decline: God specially revealed guidance, yet they followed conjecture and whim.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r1.anchor: Here the discourse has become indirect. This is a rebuke on their deprivation and misfortune

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r2.claim: Al-hudā refers to the guidance God revealed in the Qur'an and Sunnah, whose purity and exaltedness the sūrah's opening verses described.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r2.anchor: guidance which the Almighty has revealed in the form of

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r3.claim: Following conjecture is dangerous generally, and especially reckless when divine guidance is present, like leaping into death in broad daylight.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r3.anchor: following them in spite of the presence of divine guidance is like throwing one self into the pit of death in broad daylight.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r4.claim: The phrase about what souls desire specifically refers to the people's polytheistic religious innovation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r4.anchor: specifically refer to the innovation of polytheism of these people which is under discussion.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r5.claim: Every religious innovation arises from personal whim; when someone cannot meet reality's demands or easily deny reality, innovation offers an apparent escape from its obligations.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r5.anchor: every innovation originates from some personal whim or wish.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r6.claim: With no intellectual or scriptural evidence, Satan deceived idolaters that angels were God's favored daughters, that He honored their intercession, and that worship would secure worldly goods and a high afterlife status while averting accountability.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r6.anchor: Satan tried to deceive these Idolaters by saying that angels were daughters of God and that such and such daughters were especially dear to Him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r7.claim: The mythology served personal desire: it promised God's nearness and Paradise without requiring people to sacrifice what they wanted.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r7.anchor: what else is the reason behind this mythology other than personal desire and fancy?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p56/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p56/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p56/r2.claim: Their folk tale evades accountability through conjecture and fancy; conjecture cannot replace reality, and its falsity will become clear when reality appears.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p56/r2.anchor: Merely to fulfil their fancies, they are indulging in blatant conjecture.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p56/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p56/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p56/r3.claim: Zann contrasts with guidance, knowledge, and truth: knowledge may come through innate guidance, intellect, or revelation, while claims supported by none of these are baseless speculation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p56/r3.anchor: What is not substantiated by innate guidance and intellect nor by divine revelation is in fact totally speculative and baseless.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p56/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p56/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p56/r4.claim: The Arabs knew that a claim unsupported by reason cannot count as knowledge and is only conjecture without a basis.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p56/r4.anchor: The Arabs were fully aware of this reality that what is not substantiated by reason cannot be regarded as knowledge; it is mere conjecture

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p56/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p56/r5.speaker: Ṭarfah ibn al-‘Abd
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p56/r5.claim: Ṭarfah's cited line distinguishes knowledge-based knowing from conjecture.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p56/r5.anchor: The famous classical poet Ṭarfah ibn al-‘Abd has distinguished between conjecture and knowledge

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p56/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p56/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p56/r6.claim: Islahi says another aspect of conjecture will be explained under 69:20.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p56/r6.anchor: which I will inshā’Allāh explain under the following verse of Sūrah al-Ḥāqqah

QIRAAT-ER:53:23:16#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:53:23:16#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:53:23:16#1/r1.claim: The mutawatir second-person plural reading directly accuses the addressees of following conjecture, instead of speaking about them in the third person.
QIRAAT-ER:53:23:16#1/r1.anchor: 2nd person plural (you follow) instead of 3rd person (they follow)

BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r1.speaker: مولى الجامي
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r1.claim: Jāmī mocks ignorant people who give a ruined thing the name of prosperity, like a child mistaking a swelling for fat.
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r1.anchor: مرد جاهل جاه كيتى را لقب دولت نهد همنان آماس بيند طفل كويد فربهست

BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r2.claim: A satirical poem says the people of the age look human but act like predators, like wolves in clothing or clothing made of wolves.
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r2.anchor: شكل ايشان شكل إنسان فعل شان فعل سباع هم ذئبا في ثياب أو ثياب في ذئاب

BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r3.claim: The pronoun in “you named them” refers to the names, not the idols: the people made empty names rather than giving names to real deities, since these idols have no referents.
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r3.anchor: ضميرها لها لا للأصنام والمعنى جعلتموها أسماء لا جعلتم لها أسماء

BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r4.claim: The author glosses what the idolaters desire as what their evil-commanding selves covet, while also saying their ancestors fixed the names according to false whims.
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r4.anchor: تشتهيه أنفسهم الأمارة بالسوء فما موصولة ويجوز كونها مصدرية

BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r5.claim: The denied “authority” is proof for the validity of calling the idols gods; no such proof was revealed.
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r5.anchor: أي بصحة تسميتها {من سلطان} برهان تتعلقون به

BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r6.claim: The shift to third person signals turning away from the idolaters to recount their offenses to others; their naming and worship rest on deluded conjecture and desire.
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r6.anchor: التفات إلى الغيبة للإيذان بأن تعداد قبائحهم اقتضى الإعراض عنهم

BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r7.claim: The idols are only imagined forms without real referents, invented by sensual selves and weak, illusion-clouded minds; seekers and people of unveiling recognize them as nonexistent, mere propped-up wood.
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r7.anchor: نفوسكم الدنية الشهوانية وجهالة عقولكم السخيفة الهيولانية إلا أسماء صور وهمية

BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r8.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r8.claim: Created things have no independent power to create or destroy, dominate or show gentleness, benefit or harm; all beings are manifestations of divine names and loci of divine attributes of beauty and majesty.
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r8.anchor: والأشياء علويها وسفليها جمادها ونباتها حيوانها وإنسانها كلها مظاهر الأسماء الإلهية

BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r9.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r9.claim: Truth manifests in each thing according to its capacity, but in the Perfect Human it manifests in its totality, making that human God's vicegerent on earth.
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r9.anchor: إلا الإنسان الكامل فإنه تجلى فيه بحسب الكلية المجموعية وصار خليفة الله في الأرض

BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r10.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r10.claim: The idolaters fail to perceive spiritual realities and divine attributes in creation, turning instead to animal desire and bodily darkness, corrupt conjecture, and ego's preference over God's pleasure; this is manifest loss.
BURSEVI:v9p192#2/r10.anchor: أعرضتم باتباع الهوات الحيوانية وملازمة الجسمانية الظلمانية عن إدراك تلك اللطائف الروحانية

BURSEVI:v9p193/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p193/r1.speaker: الجنيد
BURSEVI:v9p193/r1.claim: Junayd says he saw seventy knowers ruined by imagining that they had truly known God; every person's grasp is limited by capacity, while God's majesty exceeds it.
BURSEVI:v9p193/r1.anchor: رأيت سبعين عارفا قد هلكوا بالتوهم أي توهموا أنهم عرفوه تعالى

BURSEVI:v9p193/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p193/r2.speaker: الواسطي
BURSEVI:v9p193/r2.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī says all knowers died in delusion, even Abū Yazīd, who also died imagining he had known God.
BURSEVI:v9p193/r2.anchor: كلهم ماتوا على التوهم حتى أبو يزيد مات على التوهم

BURSEVI:v9p193/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p193/r3.speaker: البقلي
BURSEVI:v9p193/r3.claim: Al-Baqlī warns that the spiritually conceited mistake mental images and fantasies for unveilings, insights, the unseen realm, or lights of divine power, though they are egoistic and satanic imaginings.
BURSEVI:v9p193/r3.anchor: من الأشكال والمخاييل التي تبدو في غواشي أدمغتهم وهم يحسبون أنها مكاشفات الغيوب

BURSEVI:v9p193/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p193/r4.speaker: البقلي
BURSEVI:v9p193/r4.claim: He says the Real is beyond shapes and images and warns against keeping company with ignorant claimants to seeing God; true vision belongs to saints, not enemies.
BURSEVI:v9p193/r4.anchor: والحق منزه عن الأشكال والتمثال إياك يا صاحبي وصحبة الجاهلين الحق

BURSEVI:v9p193/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p193/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p193/r5.claim: The clause about guidance is either circumstantial or parenthetical; in either case it reinforces the falsity of conjecture and makes following it worse for people already reached by revelation.
BURSEVI:v9p193/r5.anchor: حال من فاعل يتبعون أو اعتراض وأيا ما كان ففيه تأكيد لبطلان اتباع الظن

BURSEVI:v9p193/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p193/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p193/r6.claim: The guidance is the Quran and the Messenger, yet they did not follow either.
BURSEVI:v9p193/r6.anchor: فالهدى القرآن والرسول ولم يهتدوا بهما

BURSEVI:v9p193/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p193/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p193/r7.claim: In an inward reading, they ruined their uncreated innate readiness by adopting animal and elemental traits and natural darkness; despite the Prophet, Quran, miracles, and signs proving his mission, they followed desire and turned from God and His saint.
BURSEVI:v9p193/r7.anchor: إفساد استعدادهم الفطري الغير المجعول بواسطة تلبسهم بملابس الصفات الحيوانية العنصرية

BURSEVI:v9p193/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p193/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p193/r8.claim: Guidance was granted in earthly life, not in pre-eternity; whoever lacked God's light in pre-eternity will have no light forever.
BURSEVI:v9p193/r8.anchor: لأن هداهم ما اءهم إلا في يوم الدنيا لا في يوم الأزل ومن لم يجعل الله له نورا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p17/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p17/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p17/r17.claim: The statement that these are only names and have no divine authorization repeats the explanation already given for similar wording in Hud and al-Araf.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p17/r17.anchor: إن هي إلا أسماء سميتموها أنتم وآباؤكم ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان: تقدم تفسير نظيرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p17/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p17/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p17/r18.claim: Most readers use third-person ياء in يتبعون; the named readers instead use second-person تاء.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p17/r18.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: إن يتبعون بياء الغيبة وعبد الله وابن عباس وابن وثاب وطلحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p17/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p17/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p17/r19.claim: ظن is the mind inclining to one of two beliefs without proof; what the soul desires is what it leans toward for pleasure, while reason alone leads to a good outcome.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p17/r19.anchor: إلا الظن: وهو ميل النفس إلى أحد معتقدين من غير حجة، وما تهوى: أي تميل إليه بلذة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p17/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p17/r20.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p17/r20.claim: The rebuke says guidance came from their Lord while they persisted in disgraceful conduct, so they should have accepted it and left worship of idols that cannot help.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p17/r20.anchor: ولقد جاءهم من ربهم الهدى: توبيخ لهم، والذي هم عليه باطل واعتراض بين الجملتين

ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r1.claim: The pronoun “they” refers to the idols as supposed deities: in the divinity claimed for them they are only names, with no reality of godhood.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r1.anchor: إن هي ( الضمير للأصنام أي ما الأصنام باعتبار الألوهية

ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r2.claim: The pronoun in “you named them” refers to the names; naming viewed from the name means making a name for its referent, while viewed from the referent it means assigning it a name.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى : ( سميتموها ( صفة للأسماء وضميرها لها

ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r3.claim: The wording focuses on the names as bare labels without real referents, rather than on existing things that merely do not deserve those names; compare the parallel wording about worshipping only names.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r3.anchor: وإنما اختير ههنا المعنى الأول من غير تعرض للمسمى لتحقيق أن تلك الأصنام

ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r4.claim: An alternative takes the pronoun as the three names, which idolaters used because they believed the idols deserved worship, devotion, offerings, and approach.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r4.anchor: وقيل : هي للأسماء الثلاثة المذكورة حيث كانوا يطلقونها على تلك الأصنام

ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r5.claim: Al-Alusi objects that denying worshipful qualities adds little; the force of the proof is that the idols lack divinity, as the idolaters themselves generally claimed for idols.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r5.anchor: وتعقب بأنه لو سلم دلالة الأسماء المذكورة على ثبوت تلك المعاني الخاصة للأصنام

ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r6.claim: The names were invented by the people and their forefathers out of false desires, and no revealed proof or authority supports them.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r6.anchor: وضعتموها ( أنتم وآباؤكم ( بمقتضى الأهواء الباطلة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r7.claim: “They follow only conjecture” refers to their naming and worship: they merely suppose, falsely, that their practice is true; al-Raghib treats false supposition as one use of conjecture.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r7.anchor: إن يتبعو ( أي ما يتبعون فيما ذكر من التسمية والعمل بها ( إلا الظن

ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r8.claim: “What the souls desire” is a relative phrase with an omitted antecedent; the definite article may be anaphoric, possessive, or generic, and souls naturally incline to pleasures unless reason guides them to the good end.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r8.anchor: وما تهوى الأنفس ( أي والذي تشتهيه أنفسهم الأمارة بالسوء

ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r9.claim: The shift from direct address to third person signals turning away from them and reporting their offenses to others because their crimes make them unworthy of address.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r9.anchor: والألتفات في ( يتبعون ) إلى الغيبة للأيذان بأن تعداد قبائحهم اقتضى الأغراض عنهم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Masʿud, Ibn Waththab, Talha, al-Aʿmash, and ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar are among those who read “you follow” in the second person instead of “they follow.”
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r10.anchor: وقرأابن عباس وابن مسعود وابن وثاب وطلحة والأعمش وعيسى بن عمر تتبعون بتاء الخطاب

ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r11.claim: The clause “guidance came to them from their Lord” is circumstantial and confirms the error of following conjecture: God's guidance, the Messenger or the Qur'an, should have led them to truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r11.anchor: ولقد جاءهم من ربهم الهدى حال من ضمير ( يتبعو ( مقررة لبطلان ما هم عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r12.claim: “Guidance” may mean the Prophet as guide or the Qur'an, either understood as the guide or called guidance emphatically.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p57#3/r12.anchor: والمراد بالهدى الرسول صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أو القرآن العظيم على أنه بمعنى الهادي

ALUSI-FULL:v27p58/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p58/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p58/r1.claim: The clause means they follow conjecture and desire in a state that contradicts the guidance that came to them; alternatively it is parenthetical and further confirms the invalidity of their practice.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p58/r1.anchor: وحاصله ( يتبعون ) ذلك في حال ينافيه وجوز أن تكون الجملة معترضة

QUSHAYRI:v3p249/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p249/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p249/r6.claim: The names of the idols were invented by the Arabs without God's command or permission, and their worship follows conjecture and desire.
QUSHAYRI:v3p249/r6.anchor: أمركم بهذا ، أو أذن لكم به

QUSHAYRI:v3p249/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p249/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p249/r7.claim: Conjecture does not avail against truth, and the idolaters turned away from the guidance that came from their Lord.
QUSHAYRI:v3p249/r7.anchor: جآءهم من ربهم الهدى } : فأعرضوا عنه

QUSHAYRI:v3p249/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p249/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p249/r8.claim: In the spiritual path, lingering in conjectural qualities yields no reality; the way requires certainty and verification until knowledge becomes immediate.
QUSHAYRI:v3p249/r8.anchor: فليس في هذا الحديث إلا القطع والتحقق

QUSHAYRI:v3p249/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p249/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p249/r9.claim: Beautiful trustful opinion of God is not the blameworthy conjecture at issue, nor is uncertainty about one's final outcome; the condemned speculation concerns God, His attributes, and His judgments.
QUSHAYRI:v3p249/r9.anchor: أما الظن الجميل بالله فليس من هذا الباب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p409#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p409#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p409#2/r1.claim: The idols are merely names assigned by people and their ancestors, with no divine proof that they are gods.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p409#2/r1.anchor: {إن هي} ما هذه الأصنام {إلا أسماء سميتموها أنتم وآباؤكم ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p409#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p409#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p409#2/r2.claim: The passage shifts back to declarative report after directly addressing the idolaters.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p409#2/r2.anchor: ثم رجع إلى الخبر بعد المخاطبة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p409#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p409#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p409#2/r3.claim: They follow conjecture and their desires, including what Satan has made appealing to them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p409#2/r3.anchor: {إن يتبعون إلا الظن} في قولهم إنها آلهة {وما تهوى الأنفس} وما زين لهم الشيطان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p409#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p409#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p409#2/r4.claim: The guidance from God through scripture and the Messenger made clear that idols are not gods and worship belongs only to God, the One who prevails over all.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p409#2/r4.anchor: {ولقد جاءهم من ربهم الهدى} البيان بالكتاب والرسول أنها ليست بآلهة

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:21-23/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:21-23/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:21-23/r6.claim: The pronoun “they” may refer to idols: they are names applied as gods, though they contain no reality of divinity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:21-23/r6.anchor: الضمير للأصنام أي ما هي باعتبار الألوهية إلا أسماء تطلقونها عليها

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:21-23/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:21-23/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:21-23/r7.claim: Alternatively, it refers to the attributes they assign the idols, such as being gods, daughters, and intercessors.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:21-23/r7.anchor: أو للصفة التي تصفونها بها من كونها آلهة وبنات وشفعاء

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:21-23/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:21-23/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:21-23/r8.claim: Alternatively, it refers to the names Lat, ʿUzzā, and Manāt, which they chose to imply worship-worthiness, power, or entitlement to sacrifice.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:21-23/r8.anchor: أو للأسماء المذكورة فإنهم كانوا يطلقون اللات عليها باعتبار استحقاقها للعكوف على عبادتها

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:21-23/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:21-23/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:21-23/r9.claim: “You named them” means that you assigned those names to the idols.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:21-23/r9.anchor: مناة لاعتقادهم أنها تستحق أن يتقرب إليها بالقرابين. { سميتموها } سميتم بها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r1.claim: They and their forefathers assigned the names according to their desires.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r1.anchor: { أنتم وءاباؤكم } بهواكم. { ما أنزل الله بها من سلطن }

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r2.claim: The idols have no revealed proof or warrant supporting the names given them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r2.anchor: من سلطن } برهان تتعلقون به. { إن يتبعون

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r3.claim: A reading with tāʾ instead of yāʾ is also reported for “they follow.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r3.anchor: { إن يتبعون } وقرىء بالتاء. { إلا الظن }

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r4.claim: Their belief is conjecture: an unfounded supposition sustained by imitation and a false sense that their practice is true.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r4.anchor: { إلا الظن } إلا توهم أن ما هم عليه حق تقليدا وتوهما باطلا.

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r5.claim: They follow what their own selves desire.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r5.anchor: { وما تهوى الأنفس } وما تشتهيه أنفسهم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r6.claim: The guidance that came from their Lord means either the Messenger or the Book, which they abandoned.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r6.anchor: { ولقد جاءهم من ربهم الهدى } الرسول أو الكتاب فتركوه.

SULAMI:v2p286#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p286#3/r1.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p286#3/r1.claim: Junayd says he saw seventy gnostics perish through imagining they had truly known God; he connects this delusion to following conjecture.
SULAMI:v2p286#3/r1.anchor: قال الجنيد : رأيت سبعين عارفا قد هلكوا بالتوهم أي توهموا انهم عرفوه وهو قوله : ﴿ إن يتبعون إلا الظن ﴾

SULAMI:v2p286#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p286#3/r2.speaker: الشبلي
SULAMI:v2p286#3/r2.claim: Shiblī says one who realizes the Real's reality is that very reality, invoking the verse's statement that people follow conjecture.
SULAMI:v2p286#3/r2.anchor: قال الشبلي : من تحقق في حقيقة الحق فهو نفس الحقيقة لأن الله يقول : ﴿ إن يتبعون إلا الظن ﴾

BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r1.claim: The idols have no real divinity; their only reality is names applied to them.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r1.anchor: أي لا حقائق لها , فما ادعيتم لها من الإلهية ليس لها من ذلك إلا الأسماء

BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r2.claim: People and their forebears invented these names from caprice, without seeing a sign or hearing any authoritative speech from the idols.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r2.anchor: ابتدعتم تسميتها أنتم , واجتث قولهم من أصله فقال : { أنتم وآباؤكم } أي لا غير بمجرد الهوى

BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r3.claim: God sent no proof establishing the idols' entitlement to divine names or status.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r3.anchor: حجة تصلح مسلطا على ما يدعي فيها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r4.claim: Their worship rests on conjecture that idols are gods who intercede or bring worshippers near God; al-Biqāʿī defines conjecture as tipping one possibility against the conjecturer's wish.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r4.anchor: فالظن ترجيح أحد الحائزين على رغم الظان

BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r5.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r5.claim: Al-Qushayrī distinguishes blameworthy assumptions about God, attributes, and rulings from good opinion of God and uncertainty about one's own outcomes.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r5.anchor: قال القشيري : فالظن الجميل بالله فليس من هذا الباب

BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r6.claim: Because souls are deficient, their desires pull them down, whereas intellect alone urges high aims and good outcomes.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r6.anchor: وهي - لما لها من النقص - لا تشتهي أبدا إلا بما يهوي بها عن غاية أوجها إلى أسفل حضيضها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r7.claim: The intellect, rather than desire, draws people toward higher aims and good consequences.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r7.anchor: وأما المعالي وحسن العواقب فإنما تشوق إليها العقل

BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r8.claim: They received complete guidance to true religion from their Lord through scripture and the Messenger, so reason required them to follow it even if it came through an enemy.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p323/r8.anchor: الرأي يقتضي أن من رأى الهدى تبعه ولو أتاه به عدوه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p103/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p103/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p103/r3.claim: Another analysis makes the cognitive أفرأيتم suspended from taking an object because the negating إن follows; the intervening male/female clause is parenthetical.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p103/r3.anchor: ولك أن تجعل فعل ( أرأيتم ) ( على اعتبار الرؤية علمية ) معلقا عن العمل لوقوع { إن } النافية بعده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r1.claim: Ḍīzā may be a noun on the fuʿlā pattern, though its derivation makes an adjective more likely; Sībawayh says adjectives do not occur on fuʿlā with initial kasra. It may instead be a verbal noun, and either analysis has original kasra.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r1.anchor: وقيل : وزن { ضيزى } فعلى بكسر الفاء على أنه اسم مثل دفلى وشعرى ، ويبعد هذا أنه مشتق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r2.speaker: سيبويه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r2.claim: Sībawayh states that no adjective occurs on the fuʿlā pattern with initial kasra.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r2.anchor: قال سيبويه : لا يوجد فعلى بكسر الفاء في الصفات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r3.claim: The majority read ضيزى with a quiescent yāʾ; Ibn Kathīr reads it with a hamza after ḍād, reflecting the verb’s original form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { ضيزى } بياء ساكنة بعد الضاد . وقرأه ابن كثير بهمزة ساكنة بعد الضاد مراعاة لأصل الفعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r4.claim: Calling their allocation unjust adds a charge of wrongdoing to unbelief: imagining injustice resembles doing it because beliefs reveal thought and conduct.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r4.anchor: وهذا وسم لهم بالجور زيادة على الكفر لأن التفكير في الجور كفعله فإن تخيلات الإنسان ومعتقداته عنوان على أفكاره وتصرفاته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r5.claim: “They are only names” restarts the refutation at its root after reasoning from the consequences of their belief, and guards against construing the denial as merely rejecting that God has daughters or that angels are daughters.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r5.anchor: جملة { إن هي إلا أسماء سميتموها } استئناف يكر بالإبطال على معتقدهم من أصله بعد إبطاله بما هو من لوازمه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r6.claim: The pronoun هي refers to al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, and Manāt; they have no real divine entities, like the names in 12:40.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r6.anchor: والضمير { هي } عائد إلى اللات والعزى ومناة . وما صدق الضمير الذات والحقيقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r7.claim: The restriction is additional rather than absolute: the idols do have physical referents, such as stones or buildings to which worshippers go and appoint keepers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r7.anchor: والقصر إضافي ، أي هي أسماء لا حقائق عاقلة متصرفة كما تزعمون ، وليس القصر حقيقيا لأن لهاته الأصنام مسميات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r8.claim: “God sent down no authority” explains the restriction: their lack of a visible-world reality is evident because they are stones.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r8.anchor: وجملة { ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان } تعليل لمعنى القصر بطريقة الاكتفاء لأن كونها لا حقائق لها في عالم الشهادة أمر محسوس إذ ليست إلا حجارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r9.claim: The unseen can be established only by revelation from God or rational evidence, such as the world implying a maker and some attributes; God never told a messenger that idols have spirits or angels, unlike His disclosures about angels, jinn, and devils.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p107/r9.anchor: فلأن عالم الغيب لا طريق إلى إثبات ما يحتويه إلا بإعلام من عالم الغيب سبحانه ، أو بدليل العقل كدلالة العالم على وجود الصانع وبعض صفاته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r1.claim: Sulṭān means proof, and God’s sending it means informing people of it; denying that it was sent is a metonym for there being no evidence, since evidence would appear.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r1.anchor: والسلطان : الحجة ، وإنزالها من الله : الإخبار بها ، وهذا كناية عن انتفاء أن تكون عليها حجة لأن وجود الحجة يستلزم ظهورها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r2.claim: The phrase about no sign sent down evokes a road with no marker to guide a traveler.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r3.claim: Revelatory information is called “sent down” because it comes from the upper world, imagined as a body conveyed from above to below.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r3.anchor: وعبر عن الإخبار الموحى به بفعل ( أنزل ) لأنه إخبار يرد من العالم العلوي فشبه بإدلاء جسم من أعلى إلى أسفل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r4.claim: Proofs of existence are also described as sent down because reflective thought is created by God; compare 48:4, 22:71, and the earlier wording in 12:40.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r4.anchor: وكذلك عبر عن إقامة دلائل الوجود بالإنزال لأن النظر الفكري من خلق الله فشبه بالإنزال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r5.claim: The expression ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان uses a metaphorical sense of “sent down” for both revelation and rational evidence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r5.anchor: فاستعمال { ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان } من استعمال اللفظ في معنييه المجازيين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r6.claim: The extra من after the negation intensifies denial of any proof at all.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r6.anchor: وأكد نفي إنزال السلطان بحرف ( من ) الزائدة لتوكيد نفي الجنس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r7.claim: The text shifts away from direct address to the polytheists in an explanatory resumption; the pronoun in يتبعون refers to those previously addressed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r7.anchor: هذا تحويل عن خطاب المشركين الذي كان ابتداؤه من أول السورة وهو من ضروب الالتفات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r8.claim: After denying evidence for the idols’ claimed properties and names, the text says their claims rest on illusions and desires: attachment to idols, their custodians and visiting processions, and hopes for intercession.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r8.anchor: أعقب نفي أن تكون لهم حجة على الخصائص التي يزعمونها لأصنافهم أو على أن الله سماهم بتلك الأسماء بإثبات أنهم استندوا فيما يزعمونه إلى الأوهام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r9.claim: The imperfect يتبعون indicates that they will persist in following conjecture and desire, implying that they have followed them already.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r9.anchor: وجيء بالمضارع في { يتبعون } للدلالة على أنهم سيسمرون على اتباع الظن وما تهواه نفوسهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r10.claim: Ẓann ordinarily means non-certain belief, can denote certainty about unseen matters as at 2:46, and often means false belief in the Quran as at 6:116; here it means error because it generally leads to error.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r10.anchor: وأصل الظن الإعتقاد غير الجازم ، ويطلق على العلم الجازم إذا كان متعلقا بالمغيبات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r11.claim: The Prophet warns that suspicion is to be avoided because it is the most false kind of speech; Ibn ʿĀshūr gives no grading here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p108/r11.anchor: ومنه قول النبي : إياكم والظن فإن الظن أكذب الحديث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r1.claim: The Quran’s varied uses of ẓann teach Muslims to assess conjecture against evidence; scholars infer that conjecture cannot establish foundational beliefs, though sound conjecture governs branches of law.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r1.anchor: ولذلك استنبط علماؤنا أن الظن لا يغني في إثبات أصول الإعتقاد وأن الظن الصائب تناط به تفاريع الشريعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r2.claim: “What the souls desire” means what is driven only by appetite, not evidence; when evidence establishes a beloved thing, love only increases acceptance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r2.anchor: والمراد ب { ما تهوى الأنفس } : ما لا باعث عليه إلا الميل الشهواني ، دون الأدلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r3.claim: The Prophet praises two people who love one another for God and a person whose heart is attached to mosques.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r3.anchor: كما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( ورجلان تحابا في الله اجتمعا عليه وافترقا عليه ، ورجل قلبه معلق بالمساجد )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r4.claim: The Prophet says that prayer is the delight of his eyes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r4.anchor: وقال : ( وجعلت قرة عيني في الصلاة )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r5.claim: The blame falls on restricting their following to what their own desires dictate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r5.anchor: فمناط الذم في هذه الآية هو قصر اتباعهم على ما تهواه أنفسهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r6.claim: Conjecture in social dealings and moral life has different rules from conjecture in religious foundations and branches; some is praiseworthy and some blameworthy, as 49:12 says, while a saying advises vigilance toward people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r6.anchor: فمنه محمود ومنه مذموم ، كما قال تعالى : { إن بعض الظن إثم } وقيل : الحزم سوء الظن بالناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r7.claim: The article in الأنفس stands in place of a possessive, meaning “their own souls”; ما is a relative pronoun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r7.anchor: والتعريف في { الأنفس } عوض عن المضاف إليه ، أي وما تهواه أنفسهم و { ما } موصولة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r8.claim: Coordinating desire with conjecture presents their desire as the cause of following conjecture: it suits their preferences and habits.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r8.anchor: وعطف { وما تهوى الأنفس } على الظن عطف العلة على المعلول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r9.claim: The clause that guidance came from their Lord is circumstantial and intensifies the wonder that they persist in error despite receiving clear guidance from the one they must obey.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r9.anchor: وجملة { ولقد جاءهم من ربهم الهدى } حالية مقررة للتعجيب من حالهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r10.claim: The oath-like lām emphasizes the report to heighten this wonder, as their persistent misguidance might make an audience doubt that convincing guidance came.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r10.anchor: ولام القسم لتأكيد الخبر للمبالغة فيما يتضمنه من التعجيب من حالهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r11.claim: Calling God “their Lord” further marks their refusal to hear guidance as disobedience and rebellion against their Creator.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r11.anchor: والتعبير عن الجلالة بعنوان { ربهم } لزيادة التعجيب من تصاممهم عن سماع الهدى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r12.claim: The definite article in الهدى indicates the guidance’s completeness and clarity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p109/r12.anchor: والتعريف في { الهدى } للدلالة على معنى الكمال ، أي الهدى الواضح

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429/r1.anchor: ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان} أي حجة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p201/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p201/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p201/r12.claim: The descriptions that the idols are female, divine, or worthy of worship are merely names invented by people and their ancestors, with no reality or divine proof.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p201/r12.anchor: ثم قال تعالى: إن هي إلا أسماء يعني أن هذه الأوصاف من أنها إناث وأنها تعبد آلهة ونحو هذا إلا أسماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p201/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p201/r13.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p201/r13.claim: Isa ibn ʿUmar reads سلطان with a damma on its lām.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p201/r13.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن عمر: «سلطان» بضم اللام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p201/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p201/r14.speaker: عيسى وابن مسعود وابن عباس وابن وثاب وطلحة والأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p201/r14.claim: These readers use the second-person plural reading إن تتبعون, addressing the hearers directly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p201/r14.anchor: وقرأ هو وابن مسعود وابن عباس وابن وثاب وطلحة والأعمش «إن تتبعون» بالتاء على المخاطبة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p201/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p201/r15.speaker: أبو عمرو وعاصم ونافع والأعمش والجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p201/r15.claim: Abu ʿAmr, ʿAsim, Nafiʿ, al-Aʿmash, and the majority read يتبعون in the third person, reporting about the absent group.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p201/r15.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وعاصم ونافع والأعمش أيضا والجمهور: «يتبعون» بالياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202/r1.claim: ظن is inclination toward one of two conflicting beliefs without proof; desire is the soul's pursuit of pleasure, which draws it from what is best unless restrained by reason and religion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202/r1.anchor: والظن: ميل النفس إلى أحد معتقدين متخالفين دون أن يكون ميلها بحجة ولا برهان وهوى الأنفس: هو إرادتها الملذة لها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202/r2.claim: The statement that guidance came from God interrupts the rebuke as a parenthetical clause; the guidance means Muhammad and his religious law.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ولقد جاءهم من ربهم الهدى اعتراض بين الكلام فيه توبيخ لهم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿud and Ibn ʿAbbas read جاءكم, addressing the audience; al-Dahhak reports their reading جاءك in the singular instead.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وابن عباس: «ولقد جاءكم من ربكم» بالكاف فيهما، وقال الضحاك إنهما قرآ «ولقد جاءك من ربك»

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p73#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p73#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p73#3/r1.claim: The idols are merely names with no reality beneath them: they are inert objects unable to harm or benefit.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p73#3/r1.anchor: يعني الأوثان إلا أسماء والمعنى إن هذه الأوثان التي سموها بهذه الأسامي لا معنى تحتها لأنها لا تضر ولا تنفع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p73#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p73#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p73#3/r2.claim: God sent no book or proof supporting their claim that the idols are gods.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p73#3/r2.anchor: ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان أي لم ينزل كتابا فيه حجة بما يقولون إنها آلهة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p73#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p73#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p73#3/r3.claim: They follow only conjecture and desire, what Satan has made attractive to them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p73#3/r3.anchor: إن يتبعون في أنها آلهة إلا الظن وما تهوى الأنفس وهو ما زين لهم الشيطان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p73#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p73#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p73#3/r4.claim: Guidance came from God through the Book and Messenger, making their continued worship astonishing after the evidence became clear.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p73#3/r4.anchor: ولقد جاءهم من ربهم الهدى وهو البيان بالكتاب والرسول وهذا تعجيب من حالهم إذ لم يتركوا عبادتها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p458/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p458/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p458/r1.claim: The idols are names invented by people and their ancestors without divine proof; their only support is conjecture, inherited approval, self-interest in leadership, and veneration of forefathers, despite clear guidance from God’s messengers.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p458/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p458/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p458/r2.claim: Their reliance on ancestral opinion and personal advantage supplies no evidence, and they refused the clear truth and decisive proof brought by the messengers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p458/r2.anchor: ليس لهم مستند إلا حسن ظنهم بآبائهم الذين سلكوا هذا المسلك الباطل قبلهم

JISHUMI:v9p6645#2/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6645#2/r14.speaker: قراءة العامة
JISHUMI:v9p6645#2/r14.claim: The common reading has the third-person plural “they follow.”

JISHUMI:v9p6645#2/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6645#2/r15.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6645#2/r15.claim: Some read the verb with tāʾ, taking their wording in light of the preceding “have you seen” and “is it yours.”
JISHUMI:v9p6645#2/r15.anchor: وعن بعضهم بالتاء، اعتبارا بقوله: أفرأيتم .. ألكم

JISHUMI:v9p6650/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6650/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6650/r4.claim: The passage demonstrates the validity of arguing about religion, since it argues against the unbelievers.
JISHUMI:v9p6650/r4.anchor: تدل الآيات على صحة الحجاج في الدين؛ لأن جميع ذلك حجاج مع الكفار

JISHUMI:v9p6650/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6650/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6650/r5.claim: Conjecture in the fundamentals of religion is unsound; knowledge should rest on evidence and reflection.
JISHUMI:v9p6650/r5.anchor: وتدل أن الظن في أصول الدين فاسد، والواجب العلم باتباع الأدلة، والتفكر فيها

JISHUMI:v9p6650/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6650/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6650/r6.claim: The passage shows that knowledge is acquired.

JISHUMI:v9p6650/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6650/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6650/r7.claim: God’s guidance demonstrates that He removed excuses through proof, explanation, and empowerment; people turned away themselves, contrary to the coercion doctrine that God created their unbelief and deprived them of belief’s capacity.
JISHUMI:v9p6650/r7.anchor: أنه أزاح عللهم بالأدلة والبيان والتمكين، وإنما أتوا من قبلهم حيث أعرضوا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p423/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p423/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p423/r16.claim: The pronoun hiya may refer to the idols: they are only names, with no true referents, since they are the things least suited to divinity; compare 12:40.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p423/r16.anchor: هى } ضمير الأصنام ، أي ما هي { إلا أسماء } ليس تحتها في الحقيقة مسميات

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p423/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p423/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p423/r17.claim: Alternatively, hiya refers to the names al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, and Manāt; the labels express the pagans' desire, unsupported by proof from God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p423/r17.anchor: أو ضمير الأسماء وهي قولهم ، اللات والعزى ومناة ، وهم يقصدون بهذه الأسماء الآلهة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p423/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p423/r18.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p423/r18.claim: Sammaytumūhā means 'you named them by these names'; Arabic allows both direct naming and naming with bi-, as in Zayd.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p423/r18.anchor: ومعنى { سميتموها } سميتم بها ، يقال : سميته زيدا ، وسميته بزيد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p423/r19.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p423/r19.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p423/r19.claim: The verb يتبعون is also read with tāʾ as direct address.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p423/r20.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p423/r20.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p423/r20.claim: They follow only conjecture that their religion is true and their idols intercede, plus their desires; they abandon the guidance and proof sent by God, showing their religion is false.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p423/r20.anchor: إلا توهم أن ما هم عليه حق ، وأن آلهتهم شفعاؤهم ، وما تشتهيه أنفسهم ، ويتركون ما جاءهم من الهدى

MUQATIL:53:23-25/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:23-25/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:23-25/r1.claim: The idols are names invented by people and their ancestors without revealed proof; authority means a book containing evidence, as in 37:156 and 30:35.
MUQATIL:53:23-25/r1.anchor: { إن هي } يقول: ما هي { إلا أسمآء سميتموهآ أنتم وآبآؤكم مآ أنزل الله بها من سلطان } بأنها آلهة

MUQATIL:53:23-25/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:23-25/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:23-25/r2.claim: Idolaters follow conjecture and desire rather than knowledge that al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat are gods; the guidance sent by their Lord is the Qur'an.
MUQATIL:53:23-25/r2.anchor: يقول: ما لهم من علم بأنها آلهة إلا ظنا ما يستيقنون بأن اللات والعزى ومناة آلهة

NAHHAS:v4p272/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p272/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p272/r2.claim: Their claims that idols are gods and angels God's daughters have no revealed warrant; they invented them, following only conjecture and desire in naming them.
NAHHAS:v4p272/r2.anchor: قولهم الأوثان آلهة والملائكة بنات الله

NAHHAS:v4p272/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p272/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p272/r3.claim: The guidance from God makes clear that none is worthy of worship besides Him and that worship of these beings is associationism and unbelief.
NAHHAS:v4p272/r3.anchor: أي البيان بأن لا معبود سواه وأن عبادة هذه الأشياء شرك وكفر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#8/r1.claim: The idols are names without real referents, since the names have been applied to things least deserving and most unlike divinity.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#8/r1.anchor: ﴿ إن هي ﴾ ما الاصنام ﴿ إلا أسماء ﴾ ليس تحتها في الحقيقة مسميات

NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#8/r2.claim: To name them means to call them by those names.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#8/r2.anchor: ﴿ سميتموها ﴾ اى سميتم بها يقال سميته زيد أو سميته يزيد

NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#8/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#8/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#8/r3.claim: God has sent no proof authorizing their claims.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#8/r3.anchor: ﴿ أنتم وآباؤكم ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان ﴾ حجة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#8/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#8/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#8/r4.claim: Their worship follows conjecture and what their souls desire.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#8/r4.anchor: ﴿ إن يتبعون إلا الظن ﴾ الا توهم ان ماهم عليه حق ﴿ وما تهوى الأنفس ﴾ وما تشتهيه انفسهم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#8/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#8/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#8/r5.claim: The Messenger and Scripture brought guidance from their Lord, but the idolaters abandoned it and did not act on it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p189#8/r5.anchor: ﴿ ولقد جاءهم من ربهم الهدى ﴾ الرسول والكتاب فتركوه ولم يعملوا به

QURTUBI-FULL:53:23-25/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:23-25/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:23-25/r1.claim: The idols are merely names people and their ancestors carved and labeled as gods, without any proof revealed by God.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:23-25/r1.anchor: ما هي يعني هذه الأوثان { إلا أسمآء سميتموهآ } يعني نحتموها وسميتموها آلهة

QURTUBI-FULL:53:23-25/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:23-25/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:23-25/r2.claim: Their belief follows ancestral imitation, conjecture, and personal desire.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:23-25/r2.anchor: أنتم وآبآؤكم } أي قلدتموهم في ذلك. { مآ أنزل الله بها من سلطان

QURTUBI-FULL:53:23-25/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:23-25/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:23-25/r3.claim: The general reading has the third-person يَتَّبِعُونَ; ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, Ayyūb, Ibn al-Sumayqaʿ, Ibn Masʿūd, and Ibn ʿAbbās read the second-person تَتَّبِعُونَ.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:23-25/r3.anchor: وقراءة العامة { يتبعون } بالياء. وقرأ عيسى بن عمر وأيوب وابن السميقع «تتبعون» بالتاء

QURTUBI-FULL:53:23-25/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:23-25/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:23-25/r4.claim: The guidance from their Lord is the Messenger’s clarification that these idols are not gods.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:23-25/r4.anchor: ولقد جآءهم من ربهم الهدى } أي البيان من جهة الرسول أنها ليست بآلهة

RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r1.claim: One reading says their feminine and divine labels are empty names: the idols are neither truly female nor deities.
RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r1.anchor: قيل معناه : إن هي إلا أسماء ، أي كونها إناثا وكونها معبودات أسماء لا مسمى لها

RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r2.claim: Another reading says they call an idol al-ʿUzzā though it has no might.
RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r2.anchor: وقيل أسماء أي قلتم بعضها عزى ولا عزة لها

RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r3.claim: A third reading says they call the idols gods even though they are not gods.
RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r3.anchor: وقيل قلتم إنها آلهة وليست بآلهة

RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r4.claim: Razi's explanation answers their claim that angels are God's daughters: they reasoned that angels came directly from God without an intermediary, called them offspring, and inferred daughters from their feminine names.
RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r4.anchor: الملائكة أولاد الله بمعنى أنهم وجدوا بسببه من غير واسطة فقلنا إنهم أولاده

RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r5.claim: God rejects these self-invented labels because they imply deficiency; suggestive names may be used for God only when revelation supplies them, while people may not invent such names.
RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r5.anchor: هذه الأسماء استنبطتموها أنتم بهوى أنفسكم وأطلقتم على الله ما يوهم النقص وذلك غير جائز

RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r6.claim: The pronoun “they” most naturally refers to the names just mentioned: the idols' names are the labels the audience devised.
RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r6.anchor: الظاهر أنها عائدة إلى أمر معلوم وهو الأسماء كأنه قال ما هذه الأسماء التي وضعتموها أنتم

RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r7.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to the idols themselves, hyperbolically reducing something without the relevant qualities to a mere name, as in 12:40.
RAZI-FULL:v28p257#2/r7.anchor: هي عائدة إلى الأصنام بأنفسها أي ما هذه الأصنام إلا أسماء

RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r1.claim: The blame is completed by “God sent down no authority”: conventional names are acceptable only if their benefit does not carry greater harm, and implying deficiency in God is a greater harm than the benefit of these labels.
RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r1.anchor: ولا يتم الذم إلا بقوله تعالى : { ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان }

RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r2.claim: There is neither revealed nor rational authority for these names; a rational name must be free of outweighing harm.
RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r2.anchor: فلم يوجد في هذه الأسماء دليل نقلي ولا وجه عقلي

RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r3.claim: Although the names predated the audience, everyone who uses them acts like their originator; the first namer had no rational proof, so imitation cannot excuse those who follow him.
RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r3.anchor: كل من يطلق هذه الألفاظ فهو كالمبتدىء الواضع

RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r4.claim: The phrase “you named them” can linguistically mean “you placed names for them” or “you called them by these names.”
RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r4.anchor: التسمية وضع الاسم فكأنه قال أسماء وضعتموها

RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r5.claim: Razi's semantic answer is that “names you named” asserts names without real referents; “names you named by” would grant the idols an additional status beyond their names.
RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r5.anchor: إذا قال : { إن هى إلا أسماء سميتموها } أي وضعتموها في أنفسها لا مسميات لها

RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r6.claim: The comparison with Maryam does not refute this: that verse uses two objects, recognizing Maryam herself as well as her name, whereas this verse recognizes only names.
RAZI-FULL:v28p258/r6.anchor: هناك قال : { سميتها مريم } فذكر المفعولين فاعتبر حقيقة مريم بقوله { سميتها }

RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r1.claim: The bāʾ in “with it no authority” has a comitative sense, as when one says that someone departed with his family and possessions.
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r1.anchor: كما يستعمل القائل ارتحل فلان بأهله ومتاعه ، أي ارتحل ومعه الأهل والمتاع

RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r2.claim: A recitation with tāʾ addresses the audience, matching “you and your fathers”; it may be an aside to the Prophet that they follow conjecture, so he should disregard them.
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r2.anchor: قرىء { إن تتبعون } بالتاء على الخطاب ، وهو ظاهر مناسب لقوله تعالى : { أنتم وءاباؤكم }

RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r3.claim: Alternatively, the tāʾ reading addresses someone else, perhaps the fathers: when they claimed to inherit the names, the reply says the fathers themselves named them and followed conjecture.
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r3.anchor: المراد آباءهم وتقديره هو أنه لما قال : { سميتموها أنتم } كأنهم قالوا

RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r4.claim: The present tense may project a time after the speech, as in the description of the Cave sleepers' dog in 18:18.
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r4.anchor: وبصيغة المستقبل أيضا كأنه يفرض الزمان بعد زمان الكلام كما في قوله تعالى : { وكلبهم باسط ذراعيه }

RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r5.claim: A further possible subject is disbelievers generally: they follow only conjecture.
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r5.anchor: أن يكون المراد عامة الكفار كأنه قال : إن يتبع الكافرون إلا الظن

RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r6.claim: Conjecture contrasts with knowledge, though either term can be used figuratively for the other; zann itself implies obscurity, as in a well of uncertain water or a person suspected without certainty.
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r6.anchor: أما الظن فهو خلاف العلم وقد استعمل مجازا مكان العلم والعلم مكانه

RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r7.claim: Razi cites the divine saying, “I am as My servant thinks of Me,” as an apparent counterexample to condemning conjecture.

RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r8.claim: One may act on a preponderant probability when certainty is inaccessible; these idolaters are blameworthy because revealed guidance made certainty available to them.
RAZI-FULL:v28p259/r8.anchor: يجوز بناء الأمر على الظن الغالب عند العجز عن درك اليقين

RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r1.claim: One reading takes ما as a verbal noun: they follow conjecture and their souls’ desire; the verbal form points to continuing, changing desires and newly invented worship.
RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r1.anchor: مصدرية كأنه قال : إن يتبعون إلا الظن وهوى الأنفس

RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r2.claim: The verbal phrasing suggests present and future desire, not a settled past practice: they keep devising worship and replacing broken idols as desire changes.
RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r2.anchor: أن المراد أنهم يتبعون ما تهوى أنفسهم في الحال والاستقبال إشارة إلى أنهم ليسوا بثابتين على ضلال واحد

RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r3.claim: The alternative makes ما a relative pronoun: they follow whatever their souls desire, meaning the object dictated by desire rather than desire itself.
RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r3.anchor: أنها خبرية تقديره ، والذي تشتهيه أنفسهم والفرق بين المصدرية والخبرية أن المتبع على الأول الهوى وعلى الثاني مقتضى الهوى

RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r4.claim: The plural ‘souls’ is distributive: each person follows what his own soul desires, rather than everyone sharing one desire.
RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r4.anchor: هو من باب مقابلة الجمع بالجمع معناه اتبع كل واحد منهم ما تهواه نفسه

RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r5.claim: The two phrases may condemn separate domains: conjecture in belief and desire in worship; both fail because belief requires certainty and worship should oppose caprice.
RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r5.anchor: يتبعون الظن في الإعتقاد ويتبعون ما تهوى الأنفس في العمل والعبادة وكلاهما فاسد

RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, the wording descends step by step: they follow what is below conjecture, since their passions incline toward things with no good expected in them.
RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r6.anchor: أي وما دون الظن لأن القرونة تهوى ما لا يظن به خير

RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r7.claim: The guidance that came from God can mean the Qur’an, the messengers, or the miracles.
RAZI-FULL:v28p259#2/r7.anchor: { والهدى } فيه وجوه ثلاثة الأولى : القرآن الثاني : الرسل الثالث : المعجزات

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r14.speaker: author
