STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r14.claim: The second section reproaches Quraysh for idol worship, discusses its roots in ignorance and conjecture, and condemns seeking angels’ intercession.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r14.anchor: The second section (vv. 19–30) reproaches the Quraysh for worshipping idols

STUDYQURAN:53:23/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:23/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:23/r1.claim: Calling the idols names means they exist only in imagination, as Joseph says of such worship in 12:40.
STUDYQURAN:53:23/r1.anchor: as in the Prophet Joseph’s words to his fellow prisoners in 12:40: You worship apart from Him naught but names that you have named

STUDYQURAN:53:23/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:23/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:23/r2.claim: Conjecture is what one follows without knowledge, with a parallel discussion at 53:28.
STUDYQURAN:53:23/r2.anchor: Conjecture is what one follows in the absence of knowledge

STUDYQURAN:53:23/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:23/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:23/r3.claim: “That which their souls desire” refers to caprice, which wanders from one direction to another in the absence of truth.
STUDYQURAN:53:23/r3.anchor: while that which their souls desire refers to their caprice, which is the tendency to wander one way and then another in the absence of truth

STUDYQURAN:53:23/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:23/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:23/r4.claim: The phrase may be rendered more literally as “that which their souls fancy.”
STUDYQURAN:53:23/r4.anchor: The phrase could also be translated more literally, “that which their souls fancy.”

STUDYQURAN:53:23/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:23/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:23/r5.claim: Following desire or fancy means yielding to the soul that commands evil, as discussed in 12:53.
STUDYQURAN:53:23/r5.anchor: To follow that which their souls desire or “fancy” is to succumb to the soul that commands to evil

TAB-FULL:v22p55/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p55/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p55/r1.claim: The names are al-Lat, al-ʿUzza, and Manat: names the polytheists and their ancestors invented for their idols without divine sanction or permission.
TAB-FULL:v22p55/r1.anchor: ما هذه الأسماء التي سميتموها وهي اللات والعزى ومناة الثالثة الأخرى، إلا أسماء سميتموها أنتم وآباؤكم أيها المشركون بالله

TAB-FULL:v22p55/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p55/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p55/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd is cited on the phrase ‘without authority,’ referring to the linked verse in al-Aʿraf through its end.
TAB-FULL:v22p55/r2.anchor: كما حدثني يونس قال: أخبرنا ابن وهب قال: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {من سلطان} [الأعراف: 71] إلى آخر الآية

TAB-FULL:v22p55#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p55#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p55#2/r1.claim: The polytheists invented these names themselves or inherited them from ancestors who shared their unbelief, rather than receiving them through revelation or a messenger.
TAB-FULL:v22p55#2/r1.anchor: اختراق من قبل أنفسهم، أو أخذوه عن آبائهم الذين كانوا من الكفر بالله على مثل ما هم عليه منه

TAB-FULL:v22p55#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p55#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p55#2/r2.claim: God sent them guidance clarifying that the worship of al-Lat, al-ʿUzza, and Manat is improper and that worship belongs only to the one, overpowering God.
TAB-FULL:v22p55#2/r2.anchor: البيان بالوحي الذي أوحيناه إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أن عبادتها لا تنبغي

TAB-FULL:v22p55#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p55#2/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p55#2/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says they did not benefit from the guidance that came to them.
TAB-FULL:v22p55#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ولقد جاءهم من ربهم الهدى} [النجم: 23] «فما انتفعوا به»

SAMIN-DURR:53:23/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:23/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:23/r1.claim: On one analysis, هي refers to the idols: they are only names without real referents, since the worshippers assign divinity to what is utterly unlike divinity.
SAMIN-DURR:53:23/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أنها ضمير للأصنام أي: وما هي إلا أسماء ليس تحتها في الحقيقة مسميات

SAMIN-DURR:53:23/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:23/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:53:23/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes هي as referring to the names al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat: these are names the polytheists invented from desire, without proof for their validity.
SAMIN-DURR:53:23/r2.anchor: يعني: وما هذه الأسماء إلا أسماء سميتموها بهواكم وشهواتكم ليس لكم على صحة تسميتها برهان تتعلقون به، قاله الزمخشري.

SAMIN-DURR:53:23/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:23/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:53:23/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa says أسماء must mean named beings, since the verse says “you named them”; a name itself is not named.
SAMIN-DURR:53:23/r3.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " أسماء " يجب أن يكون المعنى: ذوات أسماء: لقوله " سميتموها " لأن الاسم لا يسمى

SAMIN-DURR:53:23/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:23/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:23/r4.claim: The standard reading uses third-person “they follow,” shifting from direct address to speaking about the addressees in order to belittle them.
SAMIN-DURR:53:23/r4.anchor: قوله: { إن يتبعون } العامة على الغيبة التفاتا من خطابهم إلى الغيبة عنهم تحقيرا لهم.

SAMIN-DURR:53:23/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:23/r5.speaker: عبد الله وابن عباس وطلحة وعيسى بن عمر وابن وثاب
SAMIN-DURR:53:23/r5.claim: These readers use the second-person address “you follow”; the author calls it a good, contextually fitting reading.
SAMIN-DURR:53:23/r5.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله/ وابن عباس وطلحة وعيسى بن عمر وابن وثاب بالخطاب، وهو حسن موافق.

SAMIN-DURR:53:23#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:23#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:23#2/r1.claim: In “what the souls desire,” ما can be a verbal noun particle or a relative pronoun meaning “what.”
SAMIN-DURR:53:23#2/r1.anchor: قوله: { وما تهوى الأنفس } نسق على الظن، و " ما " مصدرية، أو بمعنى الذي.

SAMIN-DURR:53:23#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:23#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:23#2/r2.claim: “Guidance has come to them from their Lord” may be a circumstantial clause describing those who follow conjecture and desire, which conflicts with the arrival of guidance.
SAMIN-DURR:53:23#2/r2.anchor: يجوز أن يكون حالا من فاعل " يتبعون " أي: يتبعون الظن وهوى النفس في حال تنافي ذلك وهي مجيء

SAMIN-DURR:53:23#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:23#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:23#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, the guidance clause is parenthetical, because the following “or does man have what he wishes?” continues the preceding phrase; the disjunctive أم is properly understood as بل plus the interrogative hamza.
SAMIN-DURR:53:23#2/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون اعتراضا فإن قوله: " أم للإنسان " متصل بقوله: { وما تهوى الأنفس } وهي أم المنقطعة

SAMIN-DURR:53:23#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:23#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:53:23#2/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the interrogative in the disjunctive أم expresses denial: man does not obtain whatever he wishes.
SAMIN-DURR:53:23#2/r4.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " ومعنى الهمزة فيها الإنكار أي: ليس للإنسان ما تمنى ".

TABATABAI:53:19-23/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:19-23/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:19-23/r1.claim: This passage’s second section rebuts idol worship and its claim of intercession; it follows proof of revelation and prophethood grounded in monotheism, and points toward resurrection and recompense.
TABATABAI:53:19-23/r1.anchor: بيان شطر من آيات الفصل الثاني من الفصول الثلاثة في السورة تتعرض لأمر الأوثان وعبادتها بدعوى أنها ستشفع لهم

TABATABAI:53:19-23/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:19-23/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:19-23/r6.claim: “They” refers to al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat as idols; the names are assigned by people and their parents, with no revealed proof of divinity, so the verse refutes their gods for lack of evidence.
TABATABAI:53:19-23/r6.anchor: ضمير { هي } للات والعزى ومناة أولها بما هي أصنام، وضمير { سميتموها } للأسماء وتسمية الأسماء جعلها أسماء

TABATABAI:53:19-23/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:19-23/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:19-23/r7.claim: “Ma” may be relative or a verbal noun, and desire means the soul’s sensual inclination; the clause condemns following falsehood and reinforces the absence of proof, while the guidance clause is circumstantial.
TABATABAI:53:19-23/r7.anchor: { ما } موصولة والضمير العائد إليها محذوف أي الذي تهواه النفس، وقيل مصدرية والتقدير هوى النفس

TABRISI:53:22-25/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:22-25/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:22-25/r6.claim: Their names for idols as gods and daughters of God are empty labels with no real meaning: the inanimate idols can neither harm nor benefit.
TABRISI:53:22-25/r6.anchor: ليس تسميتكم لهذه الأصنام بأنها آلهة وأنها بنات الله إلا أسامي لا معاني تحتها لأنه لا ضر عندها ولا نفع

TABRISI:53:22-25/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:22-25/r7.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:53:22-25/r7.claim: God sent down no book or proof authorizing their claims about the idols.
TABRISI:53:22-25/r7.anchor: لم ينزل الله كتابا لكم فيه حجة بما تقولونه عن مقاتل.

TABRISI:53:22-25/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:22-25/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:22-25/r8.claim: They follow conjecture, which is not knowledge, and their desires.
TABRISI:53:22-25/r8.anchor: الذي ليس بعلم { وما تهوى الأنفس } أي وما تميل إليه نفوسهم

TABRISI:53:22-25/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:22-25/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:22-25/r9.claim: Their Lord already sent guidance through the Book and the Messenger; the author marvels that they kept worshipping idols despite clear proof.
TABRISI:53:22-25/r9.anchor: أي البيان والرشاد بالكتاب والرسول عجب سبحانه من حالهم حيث لم يتركوا عبادتها مع وضوح البيان.

THALABI:v9p147/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p147/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p147/r1.claim: The idols are merely names invented by people and their ancestors, unsupported by any authority from God; true guidance shows that only God may be worshipped.
THALABI:v9p147/r1.anchor: إن هي يعني هذه الأوثان إلا أسماء سميتموها أنتم وآباؤكم ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان

THALABI:v9p147/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p147/r2.speaker: العامة
THALABI:v9p147/r2.claim: The common reading uses the third-person plural in “they follow.”
THALABI:v9p147/r2.anchor: إن يتبعون قرأ العامة بالياء، وقرأ عيسى بالتاء إلا الظن

THALABI:v9p147/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p147/r3.speaker: عيسى
THALABI:v9p147/r3.claim: Isa reads the verb in the second person, addressing the idolaters: they follow only conjecture, including their claims that idols are gods and intercessors, and their desires.
THALABI:v9p147/r3.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بالتاء إلا الظن في قولهم: إنها آلهة وإنها شفعاؤهم وما تهوى الأنفس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r1.claim: The idols’ names have no underlying meanings: they are inert things that can neither harm nor benefit.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r1.anchor: لا ضر عندها ولا نفع فهي تسميات ألقيت على جمادات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r2.claim: “They are only names” refers to al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat, names coined by the polytheists without proof.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r2.anchor: قوله: {إن هي} يعني اللات والعزى ومناة. يقول: ما هي إلا أسماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r3.claim: The names were falsely assigned by the polytheists and their forefathers without any warrant from God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r3.anchor: تسمية باطلة لم يقم بها حجة، وهو قوله: {ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r4.claim: Alternatively, the verse means God sent no warrant for worshipping these idols.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى: ما أنزل الله بعبادتها من سلطان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r5.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r5.claim: No scripture was sent giving them proof for their claim that the idols are gods.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r5.anchor: قال مقاتل: لم ينزل بذلك كتابا لكم فيه حجة بما تقولون إنها آلهة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r6.claim: They follow conjecture in worship, having no knowledge that the idols are gods, along with their own desires.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r6.anchor: ما لهم من علم أنها آلهة إلا ظنا يتبعون في عبادتها الظن وهوى النفس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r7.claim: Their desires are what Satan has made attractive to them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r8.claim: The guidance from their Lord means the clarification and right guidance brought by the Book and the Messenger.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r9.claim: The passage expresses amazement that they continued worshipping the idols despite the clarity of the proof.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r9.anchor: وهذا تعجيب من حالهم حيث لم يتركوا عبادتها مع وضوح البيان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r10.claim: The next passage also rebukes the disbelievers for wishing that idols would intercede for them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p48/r10.anchor: ثم أنكر على الكفار تمنيتهم شفاعة الأصنام

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:18-23/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:18-23/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:18-23/r4.claim: The idols are names without reality, coined by the Meccans and their ancestors, with no revealed proof for worshipping them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:18-23/r4.anchor: ما هذه الأوثان { إلا أسماء } لا حقيقة لها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:18-23/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:18-23/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:18-23/r5.claim: Their claim that the idols intercede rests only on conjecture and desire.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:18-23/r5.anchor: ما يتبعون في عبادتها وأنها شفعاء لهم { إلا الظن وما تهوى الأنفس }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:18-23/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:18-23/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:18-23/r6.claim: Guidance came to them from their Lord through Muhammad.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:18-23/r6.anchor: البيان على لسان محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم.

BURHAN:v1p102/r13.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p102/r13.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p102/r13.claim: The al-huda that came to them from their Lord means the Qur'an.

ITQAN:v2p410/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p410/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p410/r9.anchor: 9 وبمعنى القرآن ﴿ ولقد جاءهم من ربهم الهدى ﴾

RUMMANI:v1p76/r1.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p76/r1.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p76/r1.claim: Ijāz conveys meaning in fewer words without loss; it has deletion, which omits a recoverable word, and qasr, which packs meaning into a concise structure without omission.
RUMMANI:v1p76/r1.anchor: الإيجاز تقليل الكلام من غير إخلال بالمعنى

RUMMANI:v1p76/r5.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p76/r5.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p76/r5.claim: Qasr is more subtle than deletion because it requires knowing where compact expression works; إن يتبعون إلا الظن وما تهوى الأنفس is one example.
RUMMANI:v1p76/r5.anchor: وأما الإيجاز بالقصر دون الحذف فهو أغمض من الحذف وإن كان الحذف غامضا

RUMMANI:v1p76/r6.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p76/r6.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p76/r6.claim: Other concise forms include retribution as life, imagining every shout is against one, booty beyond reach, following desire, aggression against oneself, and evil plotting returning upon its maker.
RUMMANI:v1p76/r6.anchor: فمن ذلك: {ولكم في القصاص حياة} , ومنه {يحسبون كل صيحة عليهم}

DAMGHANI:v1p477/r13.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p477/r13.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p477/r13.claim: Hawā can mean desire or lust; Dāmghānī applies this sense to each of these passages and their parallels.
DAMGHANI:v1p477/r13.anchor: ونهى النفس عن الهوى مثلها في سورة النجم وما تهوى الأنفس

DAMGHANI:v1p472/r13.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p472/r13.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p472/r13.claim: Hudā can mean the Quran; the source groups this verse with other verses in which people receive the guidance.
DAMGHANI:v1p472/r13.anchor: التاسع الهدى القرآن قوله تعالى في سورة النجم لقد جاءهم من ربهم الهدى

DAMGHANI:v1p246/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p246/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p246/r8.claim: As names of the gods, asmāʾ means idols that people named for themselves.
DAMGHANI:v1p246/r8.anchor: الخامس : الأسماء يعني الأصنام قوله تعالى في سورة يوسف

DAMGHANI:v1p460/r11.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p460/r11.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p460/r11.claim: Nufūs here means hearts; the source likewise glosses Joseph's reference to his own nafs as his heart.
DAMGHANI:v1p460/r11.anchor: فوجه منها النفس القلب قوله تعالى في سورة النجم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p105/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p105/r1.speaker: الرماني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p105/r1.claim: Al-Rummani says ellipsis can be more eloquent than stating the answer because the reader's mind can supply many possibilities; he illustrates with omitted conclusions in two Qur'anic passages.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p105/r1.anchor: واستطرد الرماني إلى بيان وجه الإعجاز بإيجاز القصر في قوله تعالى:

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p105/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p105/r2.speaker: الرماني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p105/r2.claim: Al-Rummani distinguishes concision without ellipsis from deletion, calling it subtler because one must know where deletion is suitable; he lists this phrase among examples of concise expression.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p105/r2.anchor: واستطرد الرماني إلى بيان وجه الإعجاز بإيجاز القصر في قوله تعالى:

KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r1.author: Hishām b. al-Kalbī
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r1.speaker: author
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi locates al-Uzza in the valley of Nakhlah al-Shamiyya at Hirad, opposite al-Ghumayr on the Iraq route from Mecca, nine miles beyond Dhat Irq toward al-Bustan; Zalim ibn As'ad first built a shrine there.
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r1.anchor: وكان الذي اتخذ العزى ظالم بن أسعد كانت بواد من نخلة الشآمية يقال له حراض بإزاء الغمير

KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r2.author: Hishām b. al-Kalbī
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r2.speaker: author
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says the shrine's structure was called a bas, meaning a house.

KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r3.author: Hishām b. al-Kalbī
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r3.speaker: author
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r3.claim: The Arabs and Quraysh named people Abd al-Uzza; Quraysh regarded al-Uzza as their greatest idol, visiting it, offering gifts, and sacrificing to it, and they heard a voice at its shrine.
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r3.anchor: وكانت أعظم الأصنام عند قريش وكانوا يزورونها ويهدون لها ويتقربون عندها بالذبح

KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r4.author: Hishām b. al-Kalbī
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r4.speaker: رسول الله
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r4.claim: A report that reached al-Kalbi has the Prophet recalling that he had once offered a tawny she-camel to al-Uzza while following his people's religion.
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r4.anchor: وقد بلغنا أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكرها يوما فقال لقد أهديت للعزى شاة عفراء وأنا على دين قومي

KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r5.author: Hishām b. al-Kalbī
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r5.speaker: author
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r5.claim: Quraysh circumambulated the Kaaba invoking al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat as exalted cranes, God's daughters, and hoped-for intercessors; the revelation rejects these as names invented by people without divine authorization.
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r5.anchor: وكانت قريش تطوف بالكعبة وتقول واللات والعزى ومناة الثالثة الأخرى فإنهن الغرانيق العلي وإن شفاعتهن لترتجى

KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r6.author: Hishām b. al-Kalbī
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r6.speaker: author
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r6.claim: Quraysh protected the ravine of Siqam at al-Uzza's valley to imitate the Kaaba's sanctuary; Abu Jundub's poem recalls a woman swearing by its protected branches.
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r6.anchor: وكانت قريش قد حمت لها شعبا من وادي حراض يقال له سقام يضاهون به حرم الكعبة

KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r7.author: Hishām b. al-Kalbī
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r7.speaker: author
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r7.claim: Abu Jundub al-Hudhali's verse invokes the branches protected at Siqam, giving poetic evidence for Quraysh's shrine precinct there.

KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r8.author: Hishām b. al-Kalbī
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r8.speaker: author
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r8.claim: Dirham ibn Zayd al-Awsi swears by al-Uzza and by God whose House is at Sarif, showing the idol's role in oaths.
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r8.anchor: ولها يقول درهم بن زيد الأوسي إني ورب العزى السعيدة والله الذي دون بيته سرف

KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r9.author: Hishām b. al-Kalbī
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r9.speaker: author
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r9.claim: Al-Uzza had a slaughtering place called al-Ghabghab where offerings were sacrificed and their meat distributed among those present.
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r9.anchor: وكان لها منحر ينحرون فيه هداياها يقال له الغبغب

KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r10.author: Hishām b. al-Kalbī
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r10.speaker: author
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r10.claim: A Hudhali poet's satire about a man marrying Asma mentions driving her to al-Uzza's Ghabghab and dividing the offering there.
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r10.anchor: لقد أنكحت أسماء لحى بقيرة من الأدم أهداها امرؤ من بني غنم

KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r11.author: Hishām b. al-Kalbī
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r11.speaker: author
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r11.claim: Nuhayka al-Fazari threatens Amir ibn al-Tufayl with spears and the pilgrims' camels going to Mina and al-Ghabghab, attesting to the site's ritual prominence.
KALBI-ASNAM:v1p18/r11.anchor: يا عام لو قدرت عليك رماحنا والراقصات إلى منى فالغبغب
